stem:
A radioactive sample decays by emitting β⁻ particles.
The energy released in the decay process is the same for each nucleus that decays, but the
β⁻ particles emitted have a continuous range of kinetic energies.
Which statement explains why the β⁻ particles are emitted with a continuous range of kinetic
energies?

options.A: Some of the energy released is given to the remaining nucleons in the nucleus.
options.B: Some of the energy released is taken by an emitted antineutrino.
options.C: Some of the energy released is used to create the β⁻ particle.
options.D: Some of the energy released is used to create a new nucleon.

Which statement explains why alpha-particles have discrete energies, but beta-particles have a
continuous range of energies?

options.A: Beta-particles have a much smaller mass than alpha-particles which means beta-particles can be emitted with a larger range of velocities.
options.B: Only alpha-particles experience repulsion from the nucleus which is dependent on the number of protons in the nucleus.
options.C: Only beta-particles are emitted with another lepton and some energy is transferred to the other lepton.
options.D: Only the energy of alpha-particles is discrete because the composition of alpha-particles is always the same.

stem:
Two neutral atoms are isotopes of the same element.
Which statement about the atoms is correct?

options.A: They have a different number of neutrons and a different number of electrons.
options.B: They have a different number of neutrons and the same number of protons.
options.C: They have the same number of neutrons and a different number of electrons.
options.D: They have the same number of neutrons and the same number of protons.

stem:
A nucleus decays by emitting a β⁺ particle.
Which particle must also be emitted from the nucleus?

The nucleus of a radioactive isotope of an element emits an α-particle. The daughter nucleus
then emits a β⁻ particle and then the daughter nucleus of that reaction emits another β⁻ particle.
Which statement describes the final nuclide that is formed?

options.A: It is a different isotope of the original element.
options.B: It is a nuclide of a different element of higher proton number.
options.C: It is a nuclide of the same element but with different proton number.
options.D: It is identical to the original nuclide.
